final.title: Spot trial expiry before it surprises you
final.body:
If you run a small business, trial expiry is a bounded workflow decision, not a big AI project. The practical question is simple: when should the system flag an expiry, and who should see it first?

Start with one diagnostic question. Are your trial dates already in one place — calendar, email, spreadsheet, or CRM — or are they scattered across vendor accounts? If they are central, a light reminder rule may be enough. If they are scattered, you may need a small integration in your own environment, not a full overhaul.

Keep the decision human. Automation should surface the date; the owner still decides whether to renew, downgrade, or cancel. That matters because money movement and other high-risk decisions stay with a person. The software can notice the deadline. It should not choose the plan for you.

A useful next step is to list every SaaS trial you are using and note which tool, if any, already tracks the renewal date. That inventory tells you whether the work is simple monitoring or a slightly smarter workflow.

If you later want a build, Bareni starts with a diagnostic, then scopes a working system inside your environment. Timings are intended scopes, not guarantees.
